column2: # Phase 2 of #11 (issue #944): every openclaw install runs on a
# host prepped for the NemoClaw runtime substrate. Prereqs
# (Ubuntu >= 24.04 + docker + node) land first via a dedicated
# playbook, then the nemoclaw runtime binary via its own single-
# purpose playbook (also invocable at sync time by
# siblings currently refuse loudly per plan §7.2 (option b) — we
# still import them here rather than skipping so a darwin host
# gets a clear failure at install time instead of silently
# NB: `when:` on `import_playbook` is a static import — Ansible
# evaluates it at parse time and silently ignores the condition
# (>= 2.8). Each imported runbook enforces its own OS gate via a
# task-0 `Refuse to run on non-Linux hosts` dispatcher-contract
# guard (per AGENTS.md ""Integration Binary Install"" Rule 2). A
# darwin host reaches these plays and fails loudly at task 0
# rather than blowing up opaquely on `apt`.
# W3 (ATX iter-4): a direct `ansible-playbook install.yaml` run
# tasks and crash deep in the pair step with an opaque
# `AnsibleUndefinedVariable`. Fail early with a hint pointing at
# `clawctl agent create`, which is the only supported entry.
- name: Assert operator_platform is provided (set by core/install.py)
pair script records it on the daemon's device entry. This
playbook is invoked by `clawctl agent create`
(core/install.py), which sets it from the operator
# ATX iter-3 B2: `install_prereqs.yaml` adds the SSH user to the
# `docker` group at prereqs-time (agent user doesn't exist yet
# there); the agent user itself needs `docker` membership so
# nemoclaw sandbox tooling can talk to the Docker socket. Add it
# right after user creation so ownership of subsequent per-agent
# files sits with the right groups.
- name: Add agent user to docker group
- name: Discover openclaw binary in PATH
# W2: a zero-byte or non-executable per-agent file (e.g. crashed mid-flight
# install artifact) must NOT be accepted as a working binary — that would
# silently produce an ExecStart that crash-loops under systemd's Restart=always.
- name: Resolve openclaw binary (per-agent preferred, PATH fallback)
# The validator runs unconditionally on the RESOLVED binary — not on the
# raw `which` result and not gated on stat existence. Round 2 ATX flagged
# that gating on `not openclaw_per_agent_stat.stat.exists` creates a
# security gap: a zero-byte or non-executable per-agent file is rejected
# by W2's executable+size check, falls through to the PATH binary, but
# would then bypass this validator. Validating the resolved variable
# closes that path. The per-agent /home/... case trivially passes the
# allowlist — that's correct, not a no-op.
msg: ""Discovered openclaw binary at unsafe path: {{ openclaw_discovered_binary }}. Expected under /usr/local/bin/, /usr/bin/, or /home/.""
# Defensive parse: empty string on no-match means a version check failure
# is treated as ""version unknown"" -> not a match -> reinstall (safe default).
- name: Mark install as skipped when already installed

# A LOCAL heavy-tier serving host with no address would silently publish nothing:
# the A-record builder's truthy filter skips an empty ip, so the record the
# router chain resolves would just be absent from an otherwise green converge.
# That is the failure this repository is uniquely positioned to cause, because
# this is where the record is WRITTEN rather than merely read.
# Conditional, not absolute: an EXTERNAL runner host legitimately has no local
# address, and must not be pointed at one. The guard therefore fires only when a
# local host is named without an address to go with it.
- name: Assert a locally-named heavy-tier serving host has an address to publish
Heavy-tier serving host ""{{ llm_large_serving_host }}"" is named locally but
has no address, so its A record would be silently SKIPPED by the truthy
filter and this converge would report success while the name the router
Supply the address from tofu-proxmox's constants.serving.ip (the
destination state, published once an apply republishes the inventory
This deliberately does NOT fall back to a built-in address: a committed
default is what this change removed, and here a wrong one would not fail
locally — it would be published to the estate as authoritative DNS.
Heavy-tier serving host ""{{ llm_large_serving_host }}"" has an address to publish.
# An external runner host is a full FQDN and owns its own DNS elsewhere.
# Technitium API tokens are PER-INSTANCE — one shared token only authenticates the
# node that minted it, so the HA secondaries could not be configured. Log into THIS
# node's API with the shared admin password (technitium_install sets it identically
# on every member) to obtain this node's OWN session token, and use it for every
# API call below. Skipped under technitium_dns_apply=false (molecule/CI, no live API).
# WHY EVERY API TASK IN THIS ROLE IS DELEGATED TO THE CONTROLLER.
# technitium_dns_api_url is http://{{ technitium_dns_host }}:5380 — a NETWORK
# address. Running these tasks on the target meant entering the container over
# pct_remote only to turn around and open a network connection back to that same
# container's own IP. The container is not a privileged vantage point for its own
# API; it is just an extra hop, and it cost one SSH channel PER RECORD. The
# A-record loop alone is ~60 of them, and the paramiko-based pct_remote
# connection reset partway through every time, leaving the zone half-written and
# the run unreachable rather than failed.
# Delegating removes the hop entirely: same URL, same API, same credentials,
# one fewer failure mode. The task still evaluates the INVENTORY host's
# variables, so each member is configured through its own endpoint exactly as
# before — delegation changes where the HTTP call originates, not which host it
# This is NOT the ""delegate_to: localhost tests the controller, not the target""
# anti-pattern. That rule is about PROBES, where the point is to observe from the
# target's own position — and the two wait_for probes in ingress_and_apex.yml are
# deliberately left undelegated for exactly that reason. These are API writes
# whose subject IS the remote endpoint, so the controller is the correct origin.
- name: Authenticate to this node's Technitium API (per-host session token)
- name: Use this node's session token for subsequent API calls

### CLUSTERFORGE_RELEASE - SET THIS VALUE IN pkg/config/bloom.yaml.schema.yaml
# FIX_DNS: Set to true to allow automatic DNS fixes if DNS is broken
#          Only modifies /etc/resolv.conf if DNS tests fail AND external DNS works
#          Creates backups before modification with automatic rollback on failure
#          WARNING: Will overwrite /etc/resolv.conf if DNS is detected as broken
# PAUSE_K3S: Legacy force flag; k3s conflicts are paused automatically by default.
# Set SKIP_K3S_PAUSE: true to fail instead of auto-pausing on loaned nodes.
# DNS_SERVERS: Custom DNS servers for RKE2 cluster
#              If set, these nameservers will be written to /etc/rancher/rke2/resolv.conf
#              instead of copying host DNS. Format as YAML list (e.g., [""8.8.8.8"", ""1.1.1.1""])
# Controller/login user that should own user-facing Bloom output. This
# resolves to the pre-sudo user when ansible-playbook itself runs via sudo,
# and to USER for normal local/exported execution.
# EAI-5657: exact driver compatibility policy. These play-level defaults
# also support direct ansible-playbook use when Bloom's Go layer is bypassed.
bloom_fstab_section_header: ""# # # this section is managed by AMD Enterprise AI tool cluster-bloom""
bloom_fstab_section_footer: ""# # # end of AMD Enterprise AI cluster-bloom""
- name: Check passwordless sudo is configured
- name: Fail if passwordless sudo is not configured
❌ Passwordless sudo is required but not configured for the current user.
Fix: run the following command on the target host and then retry:
- name: Pause conflicting k3s installation (loaned nodes)
# Every notifier of ""Save iptables"" has run by this point: the port rules
# in prepare_node and the REJECT removals in validate_node. Flush here so
# the snapshot is taken while the ruleset is still only ours. Without this
# the handler runs at the end of the play, after RKE2 is up, and saves
# kube-proxy's and Cilium's live rules as if they were static config. See
# the ""Save iptables"" handler for what that breaks.
- name: Persist iptables before RKE2 starts programming them
# iptables-save is a whole-machine dump, so this is only safe while the
# ruleset still belongs to us. It is flushed after prepare_node for that
# reason. Run late, on a node where RKE2 is already up, it captures
# kube-proxy's and Cilium's live rules and writes them to the file
# netfilter-persistent replays at boot. Two things then go wrong:
#   - the replay happens ~23s before RKE2 starts, and kube-proxy's
#     KUBE-FORWARD rule needs an nfacct object that only exists once
#     kube-proxy has created it, so the restore fails with
#     ""RULE_APPEND failed (No such file or directory)"" and the unit is
#   - when it does not fail it is worse, because it replays a stale
#     snapshot of another controller's state. On one int-test node the
#     file had grown to 110 KB of KUBE-SVC-*/KUBE-SEP-* chains naming pod
# A filter-table-only dump would be the smaller blast radius, but the
# filter table is where KUBE-FORWARD lives, so it would not help. Timing
- name: Set permissions on iptables rules file

column2: # Reprovision a TrueNAS-hosted VM worker end-to-end, unattended:
#   1. configure_vms.yaml recreates THIS worker's VM with a blank zvol
#      (scoped via truenas_vms_only; other absent VMs are not recreated)
#   2. generate a full add-node ISO (`oc adm node-image create`, no
#   3. copy the ISO to the TrueNAS host, attach/refresh it as the VM's
#      CDROM (order 1005) and demote the netboot RAW below it for the
#      install boot, then start the VM
#   4. approve this node's CSRs (scoped, incl. decoding bootstrapper CSR
#      subjects) until the node is Ready, then restore the netboot RAW
# rebuild) lets this playbook sit in the linear
#   destroy — every play here no-ops (teardown already happened)
#   create  — reconcile: if the worker is already a Ready cluster node
#             the run ends green without touching it; otherwise it is
#             so an existing VM is left untouched either way)
#   rebuild — full reprovision; the node must be absent (asserted)
# E2E tested via AAP 2026-07-31 (3 rebuild cycles).
# Boot design — no netboot-pin changes required: with the zvol blank,
# the install boot falls through disk(1001, blank) -> agent ISO CDROM
# (1005; the netboot RAW is temporarily demoted to 1006 so the install
# never depends on firmware advancing past a failed iPXE exit), RHCOS
# installs and reboots, and the installed disk then boots first forever
# after. After the node joins, the netboot RAW is restored to 1004.
# The stale ISO stays attached but is NOT a usable reinstall path (its
# embedded ignition token expires within ~24h) — to rebuild again,
# - In rebuild mode the node must NOT currently exist in the cluster
# - No CSI smoke test here by design — validate storage manually once
- name: Validate vm_worker_state before touching anything
vm_worker_state must be create, rebuild or destroy
- name: Recreate the VM with a blank zvol (create-only, scoped to this worker)
# Full-ISO mode: suppress the PXE-only bootArtifactsBaseURL field in
- name: End play — vm_worker_state=destroy has nothing to provision
- name: Assert KUBECONFIG is set in the environment
fail_msg: Export KUBECONFIG before running this playbook.
- name: Discover nodes already joined to the cluster
# Persisted as a fact (not task vars) so the later truenas-hosted
- name: Record whether the worker is already a cluster node
- name: Assert the worker is not currently a cluster node (rebuild mode)
{{ worker }} is still a node in the cluster — run
- name: End play — create mode and the worker is already joined (no-op)
- name: Restrict nodes-config rendering to this worker
- name: Fetch cluster pull secret to work dir
- name: Lock down pull secret file mode
- name: Run `oc adm node-image create` (full ISO)
- name: Set fact for later plays — ISO path
- name: Attach the ISO and boot the VM
- name: End play — nothing to provision (destroy mode or node already joined)
- name: Resolve the VM definition for this worker
- name: Assert the worker maps to a truenas_vms entry
No truenas_vms entry has openshift_node == {{ worker }} —
- name: Query the VM (created by the configure_vms import)
- name: Assert the VM exists and is stopped
VM {{ _vm_def.name }} is missing or not STOPPED — expected a
- name: Copy the add-node ISO to the host
# Query the VM's devices unfiltered and pick out dtypes client-side:
# `attributes.dtype` is a path into a JSON column, and middleware
# filter support for that is unverified — an ignored filter would
# return ALL devices and a blind `first` would then rewrite the boot
# disk or NIC. Jinja-side filtering is correct regardless.
- name: Index the VM's CDROM and netboot RAW devices
- name: Attach the ISO as a new CDROM (order 1005)
- name: Point the existing CDROM at the fresh ISO
# Whether UEFI advances to the next boot entry when the netboot
# image's iPXE exits non-zero is firmware-dependent; don't bet the
# unattended install on it. Demote the RAW below the CDROM so the
# fresh agent ISO is the first fallback after the (blank) disk.
# Restored to 1004 by the final play once the node has joined.
- name: Demote the netboot RAW below the install CDROM (order 1006)
# TrueNAS 25.10 re-validates stored attributes on partial
# updates and rejects a RAW device whose image exists while
# attributes.exists is unset (""Path must not exist..."") —
# resend the attributes with exists=true alongside the order.
- name: Start the VM (retries ride out transient zvol-open error 512)
- name: Approve CSRs and wait for the node to join
- name: End play — nothing to provision (destroy mode or node already joined)
- name: Approve this node's pending CSRs and probe readiness
# Scoped approval only. Kubelet serving CSRs carry the node in
# all arrive as the shared node-bootstrapper SA with no node
# identity in the requestor, so the CSR subject CN inside
# spec.request is decoded and must name this worker — a pending
# CSR from some other joining node is never approved.
$(oc get csr -o go-template='{% raw %}{{range .items}}{{if not .status.conditions}}{{.metadata.name}} {{.spec.username}}{{""\n""}}{{end}}{{end}}{% endraw %}')
- name: Restore the netboot RAW to its steady-state boot order
- name: End play — nothing to provision (destroy mode or node already joined)
- name: Resolve the VM definition for this worker
- name: Restore demoted netboot RAW devices to order 1004
# See the demote task: partial updates must resend RAW
# attributes with exists=true or 25.10 validation rejects.
{{ worker }} rejoined and Ready; netboot RAW restored to its
steady-state boot order. The add-node ISO remains attached but
is NOT a usable reinstall path (its embedded ignition token
expires within ~24h) — rerun this playbook to rebuild again.
Deliberately NOT validated here: storage smoke tests — run one
manually once the democratic-csi driver migration completes.",samples/agreement-pilot/context/V007PILOT-MAINTAINABILITY_COMPLEXITY-036.md,,,,,,,,,,
